name: Welding
summary: Two parts of metal or thermoplastic are joined: heat melts the edges, and the melt sets into one piece. The seam can show, or be ground away.
how: Clean the joint to bare metal and fit the parts with a gap of 0 to 3 mm.
Melt the edges with an electric arc or a gas flame, and add filler rod of the same metal.
Keep the bead even, with a width of 1 to 2 times the thickness of the sheet.
Grind the bead flush for a hidden joint, or leave the bead raw for a visible joint.

origin.note: Auguste de Méritens joins lead plates with a carbon arc; oxy-acetylene gas welding follows in 1903.

adoptions.via: Car bodies change from wood frames to all-steel welded shells and roofs.
Welded steel rod makes light bases and frames for chairs and tables.
High-frequency welding joins the seams of PVC and vinyl clothes.
Jewellers leave the weld and the hammer mark in view on silver and gold.
Loft furniture shows its welds and bolts as a sign of the factory.
Ultrasonic welding seals the quartz module into the plastic watch case.
